correctness.rationale: For all m>=3 and 1<=r<=m, the open-neighbor threshold maps are reduced exactly by parity to homogeneous-or-complement cases. The proof lists and excludes all two-phase alternatives, checks fixedness and boundary r=m, proves no higher periods using strict monotonicity of a symmetric sign-bilinear energy, and proves the unique predecessor for each primitive-two phase. Direct exhaustiveness: 117 graphs, 1,834,992 labelled configurations; independent weighted counts: 1,827 graph parameters. Those finite checks corroborate but do not replace the infinite proof. Residual risk: mathematical case-split mistakes require independent verification.

originality.rationale: The exact two-parameter oscillation count and orbit isolation for all intermediate added-vertex degrees were not implied by inspected prior literature. A public previous one-leaf theorem covers r=1 and classical complete-graph dynamics covers r=m; both are explicitly acknowledged. Full texts of closest broad works concern random-graph consensus or voting-time bounds. The general Goles–Olivos period-two theorem does not enumerate orbits. Residual historical priority uncertainty persists because the original 1980 full text was unavailable.

value.rationale: A natural one-vertex extension of a clique has a complete all-degree invariant with a sharp even-order extinction threshold, odd-order onset and a central-binomial near-completion jump, plus full exclusion of transient attraction to every oscillation. It explains response to successive single-edge additions across an infinite graph family, unlike a table of small samples or a merely relabelled leaf special case. No generalized transient-time law is claimed.
